value.title: Arbitrary-center rotational classification at cardinalities 153 and 154
value.summary: Classify the possible nonidentity Euclidean rotations of finite noncollinear lattice sets and record the resulting rotational-symmetry restrictions for 153- and 154-point no-three-in-line subsets of G_77, without addressing reflections, existence, global nonexistence, or the certified interval.

value.title: Replay and audit of the 152-point lower-bound certificate
value.summary: Maintain replayable exact-integer verification of the 152-point configuration in G_76 and its embedding in G_77, while distinguishing local or governed executions from any claim of optimality or an improved bound.

value.title: Exact encoding of the rct4 154-point subclass
value.summary: Formulate and establish the soundness and completeness of the pseudo-Boolean encoding for the explicitly defined rct4 subclass, without asserting satisfiability, infeasibility, implementation-specific statistics, larger symmetry coverage, or a value of D(77).

value.title: Finite-rotation classification and its consequences at sizes 153 and 154
value.summary: Finite-rotation lemma. Let S⊂Z^2 be finite and noncollinear. If a nonidentity Euclidean rotation T satisfies T(S)=S, then T is a half-turn or a quarter-turn (in either orientation). This allows an arbitrary center; no assumption is made that the rotation preserves the whole ambient square or the whole integer lattice. Consequently, for a no-three-in-line set S⊂G_77: (1) if |S|=153, then S has no nontrivial rotational symmetry; (2) if |S|=154 and S has nontrivial rotational symmetry, it is invariant under the half-turn about (38,38), and (38,38)∉S. The result classifies rotations only, not reflections, affine maps, or approximate symmetries. The size-154 conclusion is conditional and constructs no configuration. It proves neither existence nor global nonexistence at sizes 153 or 154, does not identify the rct4 subclass with the full centered half-turn class, and does not improve 152≤D(77)≤154.

value.title: Proof of the arbitrary-center finite-rotation classification
value.summary: Proof participating in the accepted classification: differences between three noncollinear lattice points and their rotated images show that the rotation matrix is rational; the permutation action on the finite set shows that it has finite order; the rational algebraic-integer trace restriction leaves only half-turns and quarter-turns among nonidentity rotations. Orbit-cardinality and row-and-column occupancy arguments then give the stated consequences for 153- and 154-point no-three-in-line subsets of G_77. This proof is represented only for the exact accepted classification and its stated qualifications.

value.title: Replay-certified lower bound D(77) ≥ 152
value.summary: The accepted exact-integer replays certify 152 distinct points in G_76 with no collinear triple; embedding G_76 into G_77 establishes D(77)≥152. This re-verifies the existing lower bound and establishes no improved bound, optimality, or exact value of D(77). Acceptance of pinned bytes by a governed execution is distinct from the mathematical audit of the encoded predicate, and a verification request does not itself pre-assert a hosted outcome.

value.title: Replayable objective verifier for the 152-point certificate
value.summary: Pinned certificate bytes, a Python-standard-library checker, and a canonical verification request participating in the accepted objective verification. Running `python3 -I -B verify.py configuration.txt` decodes 152 distinct points in the 76×76 grid and exhaustively checks every triple with exact integer determinants. The accepted scope is that the pinned checker successfully accepts the pinned bytes and thereby re-verifies D(77)≥152. The assertion that these artifacts are byte-for-byte identical to an earlier contribution was unverified in this claim, is provenance-only, and is unnecessary for the lower bound. The tool establishes neither optimality nor a new lower bound beyond 152.

value.title: Governed replay and artifact audit of the 152-point certificate
value.summary: The included configuration.txt has SHA-256 digest a23f1f55d9a914cff49fb6ba369b9f392f7af4c5ce08085267b3af1e7d7742c4 and is byte-for-byte identical to the certificate in canonical transaction dfc0cc40d41105292a119840dcdbe6f22860cf43. The included verify.py has SHA-256 digest 43463d0207199ef42ae0dc9c88c67f855fd92b070fb8d007f477a6b2de1998ec. Executing python3 -I -B verify.py configuration.txt on these bytes decodes exactly 152 distinct points in G_76, exhaustively checks all 573,800 unordered triples with exact integer determinants, finds no collinear triple, and exits successfully; hence the bytes re-certify D(77) at least 152. The included verification.json requests a governed replay of that exact predicate but does not assert a hosted outcome before its separate attestation is published. No improved bound, optimality, or exact value of D(77) is claimed. Successful execution is established by the separate terminal attestation, not by verification.json itself.

value.title: Sound and complete encoding theorem for the rct4 subclass
value.summary: Let rho(x,y)=(y,76-x), and define the rct4 subclass of G_77 to consist exactly of sets with empty anti-diagonal, occupied off-diagonal cells equal to unions of complete four-cell rho-orbits, and main-diagonal intersection equal to exactly one antipodal pair. Give each such four-cell orbit and diagonal pair a Boolean variable, require exactly 38 four-orbit variables and one diagonal-pair variable, and for every maximal lattice line L with at least three grid cells require the weighted inequality sum_v |L intersect O_v| y_v at most 2. Expanding a satisfying assignment gives a 154-point no-three-in-line member of the rct4 subclass, and every 154-point no-three-in-line member of that subclass gives exactly one satisfying assignment. This claim makes no assertion about an implementation-specific constraint count or digest, satisfiability or infeasibility, any larger symmetry class, classification of rotations, or the value of D(77).

value.title: Pseudo-Boolean orbit-and-line encoding for the rct4 subclass
value.summary: Reusable method participating in the accepted theorem: represent eligible off-diagonal cells by complete four-cell rho-orbit variables and eligible main-diagonal cells by antipodal-pair variables; select exactly 38 four-orbits and one pair; and impose, for every maximal lattice line with at least three grid cells, the weighted occupancy inequality sum_v |L∩O_v|y_v≤2. Within the explicitly defined rct4 subclass, the variable partition gives a unique expansion of size 154 and the line inequalities are equivalent to the no-three-in-line condition. The method carries no claim of satisfiability, infeasibility, implementation-specific counts or digests, applicability to a larger symmetry class, rotational classification, or a value of D(77).
